Standard Time Line intersect each other?

[भारत का भूगोल: सामान्य परिचय, स्थिति एवं सीमाएँ • 69th B.P.S.C. (Pre),  2023]
प्रश्न (हिंदी संस्करण): On which पठार, the कर्क रेखा (Tropic of Cancer) and the Indian 
Standard Time Line intersect each other?
questions.explanationEn:
Tropic of Cancer is 23.50N and Indian standard date line is 
82.50E. Significantly, Tropic of cancer passes through eight 
states - Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, 
Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram while Indian 
standard time line passes through five states- Uttar Pradesh, 
Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. 
They both intersect at Koria district in Chhattisgarh. Korea 
district lies in Baghelkhand Plateau.

82.50E. Significantly, कर्क रेखा (Tropic of Cancer) से होकर गुजरती है eight 
states - Rajasthan, Gujarat, मध्य प्रदेश, Chhattisgarh, 
Jharkhand, पश्चिम बंगाल, Tripura and Mizoram while Indian 
standard time line से होकर गुजरती है five states- उत्तर प्रदेश, 
मध्य प्रदेश, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and आंध्र प्रदेश. 
They both intersect at Koria district in Chhattisgarh. Korea 
district lies in Baghelkhand Plateau.

and 97025' E. The Tropic of Cancer (23 030'N) divides the 
country into almost two equal parts, thus one part lies in 
tropical zone while other in temperature zone.

questions.questionTextEn:
India's territorial limit extends towards the sea up to 
how many nautical miles/km from the coast?
questions.questionTextHi:
[भारत का भूगोल: सामान्य परिचय, स्थिति एवं सीमाएँ • 68th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2022]
प्रश्न (हिंदी संस्करण): भारत's territorial limit extends towards the sea up to 
how many nautical miles/km from the coast?
optionsEn: More than one of the above
optionsHi: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanationEn:
India's territorial limit extends towards the up to 12 nautical 
miles (about 21.9 km) from the coast. Signifi cantly, the 
main land of India, extends from Kashmir in the north to 
Kanniyakumari in the South and Arunachal Pradesh in 
the east to Gujarat in the West. India's Southern boundary 
extends upto 6 0 45'N latitude in the Bay of Bengal. The 
actual distance measured from north to south is 3214 km 
and that of east to west is only 2933 kms.
questions.explanationHi:
आधिकारिक उत्तर एवं व्याख्या (68th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2022): सही विकल्प (C) है।
विस्तृत हिंदी विवरण:
India's territorial limit extends towards the up to 12 nautical 
miles (about 21.9 km) from the coast. Signifi cantly, the 
main land of India, extends from Kashmir in the north to 
Kanniyakumari in the South and अरुणाचल प्रदेश in 
the east to Gujarat in the West. India's Southern boundary 
extends upto 6 0 45'N latitude in the बंगाल की खाड़ी. The 
actual distance measured उत्तर से दक्षिण के क्रम में is 3214 km 
and that of east to west is only 2933 kms.

the Palk Strait. It is about 64-137 km wide. It was named 
after the then Governor of Madras Robert Palk.

questions.explanationEn:
Indian Standard Time is calculated on the basis of 82.5° 
E longitude .The difference between the longitude of Shillong 
and the Indian Standard Time is 92°-82.5° = 9.5° . As we 
know that the difference of 1 longitude is equals to 4 minutes. 
So the difference in time between them is 9.5 × 4 = 38 minutes. 
So, if a watch indicates 10:00a.m. on IST , then 10:38 a.m. 
would be the local time at Shillong. Thus the correct answer 
is option (b).

E longitude .The difference between the longitude of Shillong 
and the भारतीय मानक समय (IST) is 92°-82.5° = 9.5° . As we 
know that the difference of 1 longitude is equals to 4 minutes. 
So the difference in time between them is 9.5 × 4 = 38 minutes.

latitudes passes through the middle of the country). This 
imaginary line divides India into two halves. Significantly, 
the tropic of cancer does not divide the Indian International 
boundary into two halves. Notably, the maximum east-
west expansion of India does not lie along the Tropic of 
Cancer. Significantly the line joining the easternmost 
and westernmost points of India dies to the North of the 
Tropic of Cancer. Easternmost point of India is Kibithu in 
Arunachal Pradesh while the Westernmost point is Guhar 
Moti in the Kutch district of Gujarat.

The length of days in northern hemisphere, start increasing 
after the sun is moving north of equator. On 21 June (summer 
solstice) the sun is directly overhead and north pole is tilted 
towards the sun and therefore the northern hemisphere has 
days ranging from just over 12 hours around to 24 hours in 
Arctic Circle. Delhi is the most appropriate answer as it is 
the most northerly given option.

The length of days in northern hemisphere, start increasing 
after the sun is moving north of भूमध्य रेखा (Equator). On 21 June (summer 
solstice) the sun is directly overhead and north pole is tilted 
towards the sun and therefore the northern hemisphere has 
days ranging from just over 12 hours around to 24 hours in 
Arctic Circle. Delhi is the most appropriate answer as it is 
the most northerly given option.

Consider the following statements regarding India's maritime and land frontiers:
1. India's territorial waters extend into the sea up to a distance of 12 nautical miles from the appropriate baseline.
2. The Contiguous Zone of India extends up to 24 nautical miles from the baseline.
3. India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends up to 200 nautical miles from the baseline.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.questionTextHi:
[भारत का भूगोल: सामान्य परिचय, स्थिति एवं सीमाएँ • U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) / UNCLOS Maritime Law]
प्रश्न (हिंदी संस्करण): निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए regarding भारत's maritime and land frontiers:
1. भारत's territorial waters extend into the sea up to a distance of 12 nautical miles from the appropriate baseline.
2. The Contiguous Zone of भारत extends up to 24 nautical miles from the baseline.
3. भारत's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends up to 200 nautical miles from the baseline.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanationEn: Under the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (and UNCLOS 1982): (1) Territorial Sea extends up to 12 nautical miles (1 NM = 1.852 km) from the baseline; (2) Contiguous Zone extends up to 24 nautical miles; and (3) Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends up to 200 nautical miles. Hence all three statements (1, 2 and 3) are correct.
questions.explanationHi:
आधिकारिक उत्तर एवं व्याख्या (U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) / UNCLOS Maritime Law): सही विकल्प (D) है।
विस्तृत हिंदी विवरण:
Under the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (and UNCLOS 1982): (1) Territorial Sea extends up to 12 nautical miles (1 NM = 1.852 km) from the baseline; (2) Contiguous Zone extends up to 24 nautical miles; and (3) Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends up to 200 nautical miles. Hence all three statements (1, 2 and 3) are correct.
